transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I just don’t feel like myself anymore. I used to do things all the time—hiking, coaching, playing guitar, calling people back. Now I don’t really do any of it.

I sit in my little rental place for hours sometimes, knowing I should get up, clean, make a call, whatever, but I just… can’t start. It’s like the engine won’t turn over. I don’t know. I used to be dependable, you know? Protective services, schedules, radios, checklists—everything had a place. Now even answering a text feels like moving a couch.
Do you still enjoy the things you used to do, like hiking, coaching, or playing guitar?

Not really, no. I mean… I used to like hiking a lot, and coaching, and I’d pick up the guitar without thinking about it. Now it’s like those things are in another room with the door shut.

I mostly sit in my rental place and think, “I should do something,” or “I should call someone back,” but I don’t. I’ll stare at the floor or the dishes or whatever for hours. It’s not even that I decided I don’t like them anymore… I just can’t seem to start. Like I’m not myself.
Do you still find pleasure in things that you never used to enjoy, or is it that nothing seems enjoyable to you anymore?

It’s… mostly nothing really feels enjoyable. Or I don’t even get far enough to find out, I guess.

Like I stopped hiking, stopped coaching, stopped picking up the guitar. I don’t call people back. I’ll sit in that small rental place for hours, looking at stuff I know needs doing, thinking, “Okay, get up,” and then I just don’t. It’s weird because I used to be the guy who’d have everything lined up—gear in the truck, schedule set, all that—and now starting anything feels impossible. So yeah… I don’t know if it’s pleasure exactly, but I don’t feel like myself anymore.
Do you feel sad most of the time?

I don’t know if I’d call it sad most of the time. It’s more like… flat, maybe? Or stalled.

Sad sounds like crying or missing something specific, and sometimes I guess I do think about how I used to be, but then my mind goes off—like I’ll notice the trim on the wall needs fixing, and I’ll remember this old house my uncle had, and then an hour’s gone. So… I’m not sure. I haven’t really tracked it like that.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t been checking, honestly. I don’t have a scale at my place—well, I think there might’ve been one in the bathroom closet when I moved in, but I put a box in front of it and haven’t looked.

My clothes seem… maybe about the same? I mean, my belt’s always been a little weird because I punched an extra hole in it years ago, so that’s not a great measure. But no, I haven’t noticed some big weight drop or anything like that.
Do you often feel guilty about things?

Guilty… I don’t know. Not in a clear way, maybe.

I’ll think I should’ve done something, or I’ll remember some little thing from work or from years ago, and it kind of sticks for a bit. But then it turns into something else, like I’ll start thinking about whether I locked a gate or where I put a receipt, and then I’m not even on the same subject anymore.

So… often? I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say I’m walking around feeling guilty all day, if that’s what you mean.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in almost all activities you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t really feel like myself anymore.

I used to hike a lot, and I coached for a while, and I’d play guitar—nothing professional, just sitting around with it—but I don’t really do any of that now. Even calling people back, I just… don’t. I’ll see the phone and think I should, and then I’ll put it down, or I’ll start looking at something else, like the crack near the window in my rental, and then hours go by.

Some days I’m just sitting there knowing there are things I’m supposed to do, things I used to want to do, and I can’t get myself started. So… yeah, I guess I’ve lost interest in most of it.
How long have you been feeling this way?

I guess… since after I moved into the smaller rental. That was after the divorce, so… about a year and two months ago, maybe.

It’s hard to mark it exactly, because at first I thought it was just getting used to the place. The rooms are narrow, and the landlord painted over the hinges, which is strange because then the doors don’t close right—but yeah, that’s when things started unraveling, around then.
Do you feel like you're moving slower than you used to, or like it's harder to make physical movements?

I’m not sure. I mean… slower how?

Some mornings it takes me a while to get going, but I don’t know if that’s my body being slow or just me standing there thinking about what I’m supposed to do first. Like I’ll be by the kitchen counter and notice the mail stacked up, and then I’m thinking about the post office hours, and whether they changed them since that construction on the main road… and then I still haven’t put my shoes on.

But actual moving, like my arms or legs not working right? I don’t think I’ve noticed that exactly.
Have you noticed any change in how your clothes fit since you started feeling this way?

My clothes? Um… I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed, to be honest.

I mostly wear the same work pants and old shirts, and some of them were already kind of stretched out. The belt… I mean, sometimes I use a different hole, but I don’t keep track of that. I had one belt where the leather cracked near the buckle, but that was probably just old—my dad used to say you can tell a lot by the quality of leather, which is funny because he’d keep the worst shoes for mowing the lawn.

So… no, I can’t really say I’ve noticed a clear change in how they fit.
Do you often feel worthless?

Worthless… I don’t know. That’s a heavy word.

I get frustrated with myself, sure. Like if I leave something half-done or I can’t keep track of what I walked into a room for, then I’ll think, “Come on, what’s wrong with you?” But worthless, like… the whole person is no good? I don’t know if I’d say it that way.

People throw that word around too. At work, guys will say a piece of equipment is worthless when really it just needs the right part ordered, and then procurement takes three weeks because someone filled out the form wrong. So I guess I’m not sure what counts. I don’t sit there using that exact word much.
Do you often think about death?

Death? I mean… not in a planned-out way, if that’s what you mean. I don’t sit there making lists or anything.

It comes up, I guess, because with my job you hear about accidents and calls and people doing stupid things on icy roads, and then you start thinking how quick things can change. Like there was this one intersection near the old grocery store, they put in a new light but the timing is all wrong, and everybody knows it except the city, apparently. So I’ll think about stuff like that.

But do I often think about death… I don’t know. Sometimes the idea passes through, but I wouldn’t say I’m focused on it all the time.
Have you experienced any significant weight loss since you first started feeling this way?

Significant weight loss… I don’t know. I haven’t weighed myself regular, so I couldn’t tell you a number.

Like, the scale at home is in the bathroom closet behind a bunch of towels, and I only pull it out if someone mentions it, which… I mean, my brother got really into counting steps for a while and bought one of those watches, but then he stopped wearing it because it irritated his wrist. So I’m not really that kind of person, tracking things.

My clothes don’t feel dramatically different, I guess. Maybe up or down a little, but nothing where I thought, “Oh, I’m losing a lot of weight.” So… no, not that I’ve noticed.
Have you ever thought about harming yourself?

Harming myself… I don’t know. I mean, everybody says things like, “I could just disappear for a week,” when work gets stupid, but that’s not the same thing, right?

I’ve had rough days where I don’t like where my head is at, and I’ll just sit there too long, kind of staring. But actually harming myself… I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I don’t have some clear thing to tell you. It’s more like the question gets big and then I start thinking about what counts as “harm,” like not sleeping enough, or skipping meals, or when guys at work pretend they’re fine and then they end up making dumb decisions.

So… I don’t know. I haven’t really put it into words like that.
Do you feel like you're a burden to others?

A burden… I mean, I don’t know. That’s a heavy word.

Sometimes I feel like people probably get tired of me, or like I’m taking up space when everyone’s got their own stuff going on. But then I think, well, everybody needs help sometimes, right? Like at work, if one person messes up the schedule, it throws everybody off, and then suddenly you’re calling three different people just to cover one shift, and nobody says “burden,” they just say the schedule’s a mess.

So… I don’t know if I feel like a burden exactly. Maybe sometimes I worry I’m making things harder for people, but I’m not sure.
Do you feel like your current state is interfering with your daily life most of the time?

Yeah… I mean, most of the time, yes, probably.

It’s not just like having a bad week and then you get back into your routine. I was suspended from work — protective service work — after this routine patrol where I… I scared some staff and people standing around. It wasn’t supposed to be anything, just normal rounds, and then suddenly everyone’s looking at me like I’m the problem.

And since then, things kind of collapsed outward. I used to coach a bit, volunteer, people would call me because they knew I’d show up. Now I don’t really do much of that. I’ve pulled back from most people. It’s easier not to explain, because once you start explaining, they ask more questions, and then you’re standing there in a grocery aisle talking about your whole life when all you wanted was cereal.

So yes… it’s interfering. More than I like to admit.
Do you feel like your lack of interest in activities is present every day?

Yeah… most days, I think. It’s not like I wake up and decide, “I’m not interested in anything today.” It’s more like everything just sort of… doesn’t reach me.

I used to hike, coach, play guitar a little, call people back when they left messages. I had things. Now I’ll be in that small rental place and I’ll know there are things I should do, even simple things, and I just sit there for hours. Like I’m waiting for the engine to turn over, but it doesn’t.

Some days I tell myself it’s just being tired, or it’s the weather, or everybody gets in a rut. My old hiking boots are still by the door, actually, which is stupid because I’m not using them, and they get in the way when I bring groceries in. But moving them feels like admitting something.

So… yeah. It’s there pretty much every day.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure most of the time?

Most of the time, yeah… I think that’s fair to say.

It’s not that nothing is ever nice, exactly. Like, coffee still tastes like coffee, and sometimes there’s a good song on somewhere — though I don’t really play guitar anymore, which is funny because I used to keep it right by the couch, and now it’s just kind of… there.

Mostly I just don’t feel like myself anymore. I stopped hiking, stopped coaching, stopped calling people back. Some days I sit in that small rental for hours knowing there are things I should do, even easy things, and I just can’t get myself to start.

So pleasure… I don’t know. It’s like it’s supposed to be there, but it doesn’t land the way it used to.
Do you feel like your current state is severely impairing your ability to function in daily life?

Yeah… severely, I guess. I don’t like that word, but it fits.

I mean, I got suspended from my protective service job after that patrol where I scared staff and some people standing around, and it was supposed to be routine — just walking through, checking things like I’d done a hundred times. And then suddenly it’s reports and meetings and everyone talking in those careful voices.

After that, I just… stopped being the person people could count on. I’m not coaching now, not volunteering. People used to call me because I’d show up, you know? Like if someone needed help moving a table or running drills or covering something, I was the guy. Now I avoid calls half the time.

So daily life, yeah. It’s not just inconvenient. It’s like the whole structure came apart.
Do you feel like your current state is severely impairing your social relationships?

Yeah… it has. I mean, people still say “just call me” or “come by,” but after what happened at work, after I got suspended from protective service because I scared staff and people nearby on what was supposed to be a normal patrol… it’s like everyone started standing a little farther away.

And I guess I did too. I pulled back from coaching, from volunteering, from the people who used to count on me. I used to be the reliable one, the guy who showed up early and stayed late, you know? My old coach used to say that mattered more than talent — showing up. Funny thing, I still remember him saying it by the equipment shed, because the door never latched right—

But, yeah. Social relationships. They’re pretty badly affected. I don’t answer people like I should. I avoid them. I think they don’t know what to do with me now, and honestly I don’t know what to do with them either.

doctor.question: Do you feel like your lack of interest in activities is present every day?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: Mostly I just don't feel like myself anymore—I stopped hiking, coaching, playing guitar, and calling people back, and some days I sit in that small rental for hours knowing there are things to do but I can't make myself start.
target_item.reason: The question asks about lack of interest in activities being present every day, which directly relates to diminished motivation and social/activity interest.

patient.answer:
Yeah… most days, I think. It’s not like I wake up and decide, “I’m not interested in anything today.” It’s more like everything just sort of… doesn’t reach me.

I used to hike, coach, play guitar a little, call people back when they left messages. I had things. Now I’ll be in that small rental place and I’ll know there are things I should do, even simple things, and I just sit there for hours. Like I’m waiting for the engine to turn over, but it doesn’t.

Some days I tell myself it’s just being tired, or it’s the weather, or everybody gets in a rut. My old hiking boots are still by the door, actually, which is stupid because I’m not using them, and they get in the way when I bring groceries in. But moving them feels like admitting something.

So… yeah. It’s there pretty much every day.

doctor.intent: determine the severity of depressive symptoms
doctor.question: Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure most of the time?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: Mostly I just don't feel like myself anymore—I stopped hiking, coaching, playing guitar, and calling people back, and some days I sit in that small rental for hours knowing there are things to do but I can't make myself start.
target_item.reason: The question asks about inability to experience pleasure most of the time, which is anhedonia and fits the negative symptoms profile, including diminished interest and enjoyment in activities.

patient.answer:
Most of the time, yeah… I think that’s fair to say.

It’s not that nothing is ever nice, exactly. Like, coffee still tastes like coffee, and sometimes there’s a good song on somewhere — though I don’t really play guitar anymore, which is funny because I used to keep it right by the couch, and now it’s just kind of… there.

Mostly I just don’t feel like myself anymore. I stopped hiking, stopped coaching, stopped calling people back. Some days I sit in that small rental for hours knowing there are things I should do, even easy things, and I just can’t get myself to start.

So pleasure… I don’t know. It’s like it’s supposed to be there, but it doesn’t land the way it used to.

doctor.question: Do you feel like your current state is severely impairing your ability to function in daily life?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I got suspended from protective service work after I scared staff and bystanders during a routine patrol, and since then I’ve pulled away from coaching, volunteering, and most of the people who used to count on me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the current state severely impairs daily functioning, which directly matches the functional impairment profile.

patient.answer:
Yeah… severely, I guess. I don’t like that word, but it fits.

I mean, I got suspended from my protective service job after that patrol where I scared staff and some people standing around, and it was supposed to be routine — just walking through, checking things like I’d done a hundred times. And then suddenly it’s reports and meetings and everyone talking in those careful voices.

After that, I just… stopped being the person people could count on. I’m not coaching now, not volunteering. People used to call me because I’d show up, you know? Like if someone needed help moving a table or running drills or covering something, I was the guy. Now I avoid calls half the time.

So daily life, yeah. It’s not just inconvenient. It’s like the whole structure came apart.

doctor.intent: determine the severity of depressive symptoms
doctor.question: Do you feel like your current state is severely impairing your social relationships?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I got suspended from protective service work after I scared staff and bystanders during a routine patrol, and since then I’ve pulled away from coaching, volunteering, and most of the people who used to count on me.
target_item.reason: The question asks whether the current state is severely impairing social relationships, which is directly about impairment in functioning, including pulling away from coaching, volunteering, and people who used to count on me.

patient.answer:
Yeah… it has. I mean, people still say “just call me” or “come by,” but after what happened at work, after I got suspended from protective service because I scared staff and people nearby on what was supposed to be a normal patrol… it’s like everyone started standing a little farther away.

And I guess I did too. I pulled back from coaching, from volunteering, from the people who used to count on me. I used to be the reliable one, the guy who showed up early and stayed late, you know? My old coach used to say that mattered more than talent — showing up. Funny thing, I still remember him saying it by the equipment shed, because the door never latched right—

But, yeah. Social relationships. They’re pretty badly affected. I don’t answer people like I should. I avoid them. I think they don’t know what to do with me now, and honestly I don’t know what to do with them either.
